<feature feature-id="CC-0069">
  <title>Add JSON schema for Helm chart values</title>
  <description># GitHub Issue #189: Add JSON schema for Helm chart values

**Category**: improvement | **Scope**: Medium

**Description**: Create a values.schema.json file for the Helm chart that validates all values.yaml fields with proper types, constraints, descriptions, and defaults. Include constraints like minimum replica counts, valid log levels, valid image pull policies, port ranges, and resource request/limit formats. Reference it from Chart.yaml.

**Motivation**: Without a JSON schema, users can set invalid values (e.g., replicas: -1, logLevel: 'verbose') without any feedback until Helm template rendering or runtime failure. A schema provides IDE autocompletion, early validation during helm install/upgrade, and serves as living documentation of all configuration options.

**Affected Areas**:
- `operators/keystone/charts/keystone-operator/`

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] values.schema.json covers all fields in values.yaml
- [ ] Schema enforces type constraints, enums for known value sets, and min/max where applicable
- [ ] helm install with invalid values produces a clear validation error
- [ ] IDE autocompletion works with the schema in VS Code with the Helm extension
- [ ] Schema is referenced in Chart.yaml

---
Source: https://github.com/C5C3/forge/issues/189</description>

  <implementation-notes>Architecture: Single values.schema.json file placed at operators/keystone/helm/keystone-operator/values.schema.json alongside Chart.yaml and values.yaml. Helm auto-discovers this file. No code changes to templates needed.

Schema structure mirrors values.yaml hierarchy:
- Root object with additionalProperties: false
- image: { repository (string), tag (string), pullPolicy (enum) }
- replicas: integer, minimum 1
- resources: { limits: { cpu, memory }, requests: { cpu, memory } } with K8s quantity patterns
- rbac: { namespaceScoped (boolean) }
- leaderElection: { enabled (boolean) }
- webhook: { enabled (boolean) }
- metrics: { port (integer, 1-65535) }
- serviceAccount: { create (boolean), name (string) }
- nameOverride: string (optional, from _helpers.tpl)
- fullnameOverride: string (optional, from _helpers.tpl)

Potential pitfall: helm-unittest sets values via 'set:' blocks which internally go through schema validation. Ensure the schema allows all value combinations used in existing tests. Verify by running helm unittest after adding schema.

K8s resource quantity pattern: Use a permissive regex that covers the common formats (integer, decimal, millicpu suffix, binary/SI memory suffixes) without being overly strict.</implementation-notes>
</feature>

  <stories>
    <story title="Operator deployer gets early validation of Helm values">As a operator deployer, I want Helm to reject invalid values at install/upgrade time before any templates are rendered, so that I catch configuration errors immediately rather than debugging runtime failures</story>
    <story title="Chart developer gets IDE autocompletion for values">As a chart developer, I want my IDE to provide autocompletion and inline documentation for all values.yaml fields, so that I can discover available configuration options without reading source templates</story>
    <story title="Operator deployer gets validation of type constraints">As a operator deployer, I want the schema to enforce correct types for all values fields, so that type mismatches (e.g., string where integer expected) are caught before deployment</story>
    <story title="Operator deployer provides valid resource requests and limits">As a operator deployer, I want the schema to accept valid Kubernetes resource quantity formats for CPU and memory, so that I can use standard Kubernetes resource notation (e.g., 500m, 128Mi) without false rejections</story>
    <story title="CI pipeline validates chart with schema">As a CI system, I want helm lint to automatically validate the schema is well-formed and consistent with values.yaml, so that schema drift from values.yaml is caught in the existing CI helm-validate job</story>
  </stories>

    <requirement id="REQ-003" priority="SHALL">The schema SHALL enforce enum constraints for fields with a known set of valid values</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-004" priority="SHALL">The schema SHALL enforce minimum/maximum constraints where semantically appropriate</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-005" priority="SHALL">The schema SHALL include a description field for every property to serve as living documentation</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-006" priority="SHALL">The schema SHALL specify default values that match values.yaml defaults</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-007" priority="SHALL">Chart.yaml SHALL reference the schema file so Helm and tooling discover it automatically</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-008" priority="SHALL">The schema SHALL use additionalProperties: false at each object level to reject unknown fields</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-009" priority="SHALL">The schema SHALL validate Kubernetes resource quantity strings with an appropriate pattern</requirement>
    <requirement id="REQ-010" priority="SHALL">Existing CI helm-validate job SHALL continue to pass with the schema in place</requirement>
  </requirements>
